dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:6001.text: What remains hard. Formed from 石 and abbreviated 堅.

shuowen:6002.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 厤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6003.text: A crag, 礹: stone. Formed from 石, with 斬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6004.text: A rocky mountain. Formed from 石, with 嚴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6005.text: Hard. Formed from 石, with 毄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6006.text: Hard stone. Formed from 石, with 角 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6007.text: Hard stone. Formed from 石, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6008.text: A rocky crag. Formed from 石, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6009.text: A crag, 磛嵒. Formed from 石 and 品. The Book of Zhou says: “Fear the people’s precipitous temper.” Pronounced the same as 巖.

shuowen:6010.text: A musical stone. Formed from 石 and 殸, depicting suspension from a frame; 殳 strikes it. In antiquity the Muju clan made the chime stone.

shuowen:6011.text: To stop. Formed from 石, with 疑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6012.text: To pick 空青 mineral and coral from a cliff above and dislodge them; the recorded activity is uncertain. Formed from 石, with 折 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou has the 硩蔟 officer.

shuowen:6013.text: To smooth silk with stone. Formed from 石, with 延 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6014.text: To grind. Formed from 石, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6015.text: Stone broken. Formed from 石, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6016.text: To grind smooth. Formed from 石, with 龍 indicating the sound. The Son of Heaven’s rafters are hewn and then polished.

shuowen:6017.text: To grind. Formed from 石, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6018.text: A stone mill. Formed from 石, with 靡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6019.text: A mill. Formed from 石, with 豈 indicating the sound. In antiquity Gongshu Ban made the mill.

shuowen:6020.text: To pound grain. Formed from 石, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6021.text: Pounding again after the grain has already been pounded is 䂿. Formed from 石, with 沓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6022.text: A stone attached to the cord of a shooting arrow. Formed from 石, with 番 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6023.text: To chop. Formed from 石, with 箸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6024.text: A smooth stone. Formed from 石, with 見 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6025.text: To puncture an afflicted part with stone. Formed from 石, with 乏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6026.text: Stone; poor or bad. Formed from 石, with 鬲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6027.text: Stones in a heap, 磊砢. Formed from 石, with 可 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6028.text: Many stones. Formed from three 石.

shuowen:6029.text: To grind or sharpen. Formed from 石, with 厲 indicating the sound. The classics also use 厲.

shuowen:6030.text: The Zuo Commentary mentions “Shi Que, a grand officer of Wei.” The Tangyun says it means respectful. Formed from 石; further details are unknown. 昔 indicates the sound.

shuowen:6031.text: A large rock against which water surges. Formed from 石, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6032.text: The appearance of stone. Formed from 石, with 彔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6033.text: A stone supporting block. Formed from 石, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6034.text: Masonry on steps. Formed from 石, with 切 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6035.text: A stone beneath a pillar. Formed from 石, with 質 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6036.text: A pillar-base stone, 礩. Formed from 石, with 楚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6037.text: To pound. Formed from 石, with 垂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6038.text: Long in time or distance. Formed from 兀 and 匕; 兀 conveys height and distance. Over time things change. 亾 indicates the sound; 纼 is inverted 亾. All characters in this group are formed from 長. The recorded identification of 纼 is uncertain.

shuowen:6039.text: An utmost limit; to set out. Formed from 長, with 隶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6040.text: Long-lasting. Formed from 長, with 爾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6041.text: A snake’s virulent poison extending; the wording 惡毒長 is uncertain. Formed from 長, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6042.text: A flag erected in districts and neighborhoods. Depicts its staff and three streamers, of mixed silks with each half-width different. It urges the people on; hence haste is called 勿勿. All characters in this group are formed from 勿.

shuowen:6043.text: To open. Formed from 日, 一 and 勿. Another explanation: to fly aloft. Another: long. Another: the appearance of many strong people.

shuowen:6044.text: Hair drooping, 冄冄. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 冄.

shuowen:6045.text: Cheek hair. Depicts hair. The Rites of Zhou says: “Make its scales and its beard.” All characters in this group are formed from 而.

shuowen:6046.text: A punishment not severe enough to require shaving the head. Formed from 而 and 彡.

shuowen:6047.text: A pig, 彘. Its tail ends, hence called 豕; the phrase 竭其尾 is uncertain. Depicts hair, feet and a tail behind. Pronounced the same as 豨. Note: contemporary writing wrongly uses 豕 for 彘 and 彘 for 豕. How is this clear? 啄 and 琢 follow 豕, while 蟸 follows 彘; all take their sounds from these, making the distinction clear. All characters in this group are formed from 豕.

shuowen:6048.text: A pig whose hairs cluster in threes. Formed from 豕, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6049.text: A small piglet. Formed from 豕, with 𣪎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6050.text: A three-month-old piglet, its belly bulging, 豯豯. Formed from 豕, with 奚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6051.text: A six-month-old piglet. Formed from 豕, with 從 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a one-year-old pig, still gathering in a group.

shuowen:6052.text: A sow. Formed from 豕, with 巴 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a one-year-old pig able to seize or grapple with another. The Odes says: “One shot, five sows.”

shuowen:6053.text: A three-year-old pig, its shoulders having reached full height. Formed from 豕, with 幵 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Drive side by side after two three-year-old boars.”

shuowen:6054.text: A castrated pig. Formed from 豕, with 賁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6055.text: A male pig. Formed from 豕, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6056.text: Shanggu’s name for a boar. Formed from 豕, with abbreviated 役 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6057.text: A castrated pig. Formed from 豕, with 隋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6058.text: To bite. Formed from 豕, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6059.text: A pig’s breathing. Formed from 豕, with 壹 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “He begot Ao and Yi.”

shuowen:6060.text: A pig’s breathing. Formed from 豕, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6061.text: To raise pigs in pens on grain. Formed from 豕, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6062.text: A kind of pig. Formed from 豕, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6063.text: To escape or run free. Formed from 豕, with 原 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “The 豲 has claws but dares not scratch with them.” Read like 桓.

shuowen:6064.text: A pig running, 豨豨. Formed from 豕, with 希 indicating the sound. In antiquity there was the scourge of giant boars and long snakes.

shuowen:6065.text: A pig walking with bound feet, 豖豖. Formed from 豕 with two feet tied.

shuowen:6066.text: To fight locked together without separating. Formed from 豕 and 虍: a pig and tiger fighting without separating. Read like 蘮 in the plant name 蘮蒘. Sima Xiangru says 豦 is a kind of giant boar. Another explanation: a tiger raising two feet.

shuowen:6067.text: A pig angry with its hairs erect. Another explanation: to cut down or destroy. Formed from 豕 and 辛.

shuowen:6068.text: Two pigs. 豳 follows this element. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:6069.text: A long-bristled beast. Another explanation: Henei’s name for a pig. Formed from 彑, with the lower part depicting hairy feet. All characters in this group are formed from 㣇. Read like 弟.

shuowen:6070.text: A kind of pig. Formed from 㣇, with 曶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6071.text: A pig whose bristles resemble brush tubes, from Nan Commandery. Formed from 㣇, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6072.text: A creature resembling a porcupine. Formed from 㣇, with abbreviated 胃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6073.text: A kind of 㣇 beast. Formed from two 㣇.

shuowen:6074.text: A pig’s head, depicting its pointed shape seen above. All characters in this group are formed from 彑. Read like 罽.

shuowen:6075.text: A pig. A pig with disabled rear hooves is called 彘. Formed from 彑, with 矢 indicating the sound, and two 匕: a pig’s feet are the same as a deer’s.

shuowen:6076.text: A pig. Formed from 彑 and 豕. Read like 弛.

shuowen:6077.text: A pig. Formed from 彑, with the lower part depicting its feet. Read like 瑕.

shuowen:6078.text: A pig running. Formed from 彑 and abbreviated 豕.

shuowen:6079.text: A small pig. Formed from abbreviated 彖; pictographic. Also formed from 又 holding 肉, to supply sacrifices. All characters in this group are formed from 豚.

shuowen:6080.text: A kind of piglet. Formed from 豚, with 衞 indicating the sound. Read like 罽.

shuowen:6081.text: A long-backed beast moving stealthily, 豸豸, as if watching to kill something. All characters in this group are formed from 豸. In 司殺, 司 is read like 伺 in 伺候.

shuowen:6082.text: Resembles a tiger, with round markings. Formed from 豸, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6083.text: 貙獌, resembling a 貍 beast. Formed from 豸, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6084.text: A kind of 貙 beast. Formed from 豸, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6085.text: A leopard-like beast from Mo country, 貉國. Formed from 豸, with 𣬉 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Present its 貔 skin.” The Book of Zhou says: “Like tigers, like 貔.” 貔 is a fierce beast.

shuowen:6086.text: A wolf-like beast with a dog’s voice. Formed from 豸, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6087.text: 猰貐, resembling a 貙, with tiger’s claws; it eats people and runs swiftly. Formed from 豸, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6088.text: Resembles a bear, yellow and black, from Shu. Formed from 豸, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6089.text: A fierce beast. Formed from 豸, with 庸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6090.text: 纱玃, perhaps a large ape; the recorded animal name is uncertain. Formed from 豸, with 矍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6091.text: A beast without forefeet. Formed from 豸, with 出 indicating the sound. Han law: “For catching a jackal or 貀, a reward of one hundred coins.”

shuowen:6092.text: A fox-like beast fond of sleeping. Formed from 豸, with 舟 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Thick fox and 貈 furs for dwelling at home.”

shuowen:6093.text: A wild dog of Hu territory. Formed from 豸, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6094.text: A rodent-like beast, large, yellow and black, from the Hu state of Dingling. Formed from 豸, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6095.text: A northern kind of beast. Formed from 豸, with 各 indicating the sound. Confucius says: “貉 conveys the meaning of evil.”

shuowen:6096.text: A kind of 貉 beast. Formed from 豸, with 亘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6097.text: A lurking beast resembling a 貙. Formed from 豸, with 里 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6098.text: A beast. Formed from 豸, with 耑 indicating the sound. Read like 湍.

shuowen:6099.text: A wild pig. Formed from 豸, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6100.text: A rodent-like beast, good at turning about. Formed from 豸, with 穴 indicating the sound.
